title: Finding All Students and All Courses: FULL JOIN

blocks.content: Finding All Students and All Courses: FULL JOIN

To answer the dean's question, "Can we get a comprehensive view of all students and all courses, even if they don't match?" you can combine the Students and Courses tables via the Enrollments table to display all students and all courses in a single result.
For this, a FULL JOIN is ideal because it includes all records from both tables, showing unmatched rows with NULL values for a complete view of all students and courses.

1-- Include all students and all courses,
2-- showing NULL where relationships are
3-- missing.
4
5SELECT 
6    Students.id student_id,
7    Students.name student_name,
8    Courses.id course_id,
9    Courses.course_name
10FROM 
11    Students
12FULL JOIN Enrollments ON Students.id = Enrollments.student_id
13FULL JOIN Courses ON Enrollments.course_id = Courses.id;

items: Jack Miller appears with NULL under course_id and course_name, indicating he's not enrolled in any course.
Python Programming (C104) appears with NULL under student_id and student_name, indicating no students are enrolled in this course.
Students like Alice Johnson and Carol Davis appear with their respective course details, showing they are enrolled.
